commits.subject: AMX attention kernels for 256-dim heads with 4 query heads per KV head

summary:
Short version: Part B is implemented in one commit on jhan-gdn-partb (base 72e1191804). The new 256 x 4 kernels pass their error-band tests on delphi-3b35 with AMX really executing, and runtron of the one-model tree calls them. Task 4 passes its rule: with the data in cache the AMX path is 2.34 to 2.72 times faster than the AVX-512 path (rule: 1.5 or more), at a core clock of 2.40 GHz against 2.70 GHz.

WHAT WAS BUILT (line numbers at the head commit)
- h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:254-315: second namespace tron::amx_attn_h256g4 with HEAD_SIZE_256, Q_PACK_ELEMS_4096, shape_ok, eligible, and the three kernel declarations. It imports TILE_ROWS_16, TILE_ROW_BYTES_64, PAGE_TOKENS_64, GROUP_HEADS_4 and query_scalar_ok from amx_attn_h128g4. The file header, Note [AMX attention dispatch] and Note [Tile stores write 16 rows] now describe two shapes. amx_attn_h128g4::shape_ok (line 154) is unchanged, so amx_attn_h128g4::eligible stays false for (256, 4).
- src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:280-508: the 256 x 4 kernels. git numstat for this file is 233 added, 0 deleted, so the three 128 x 4 bodies are byte for byte as before. pack_q_group_256x4 (397): 8 panels. qk_rowmajor_256x4 (421): 8 dim steps of 32 into the same 4 accumulator tiles, 32 tile products, 40 tile loads, 4 tile stores. weights_times_v_256x4 (464): 4 groups of 64 output dims, 32 tile products, 40 tile loads, 16 tile stores. Two file-local helpers hold the shape-independent parts: store_query_rows (339, the transposing store) and weights_to_bf16 (381, the weight rounding).
- available(), begin_region(), end_region() are still the single functions of amx_attn_h128g4. Both shapes call them by that name.
- h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp: class-level gates amx_serves_128x4 / amx_serves_256x4 / amx_serves (227-236) replace the three spelled-out gate expressions (1564, 1784, 1930). The slot size amx_q_pack_elems (241) is the largest pack among plugin::attention_kernels, so a model without a 256 x 4 kernel keeps 4096-byte slots (291). packed_amx_query selects the packer by shape and has a static_assert per branch that the packer fits the slot (1726-1737). apply_dense_amx_page selects the QK and PV kernel by shape (1802, 1834).
- Resize trap: self_attention.hpp:1583 is now "if (amx_qpack.size() < items.size()) amx_qpack.resize(items.size());". The array only grows, so a small minibatch followed by a large one does not zero-fill the slots again. This line also runs for 128 x 4 models.
- Attention statistics: no new counter. The 256 arm of t_amx_dispatch_dtype checks one amx visit and 64 amx K tokens per call for a full 256-dim page, and an avx visit with 63 K tokens for a partial page.
- Tests: t/t_amx_numerics.cpp runs the packer layout case and the QK and PV error-band cases as TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE over shape_128x4 and shape_256x4 (173, 209, 259), with the same method and tolerances. The gate case adds the 256 gate and the two cross-shape rejections (159-170). t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp defines fakes for the three new entry points (282-309), takes the head size as a template parameter (86), and adds two 256-dim sections (337, 342). A new probe field wrong_shape_calls (60, 206) fails the test when a call reaches the kernels of the other shape.
- Comments: h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp names both PV kernels as layout-specific readers. t/CMakeLists.txt comment names both namespaces.

CHOICES TAKEN (smaller diff where the change list left a choice)
- Second namespace with non-template _256x4 entry points, as the report recommends.
- available/begin_region/end_region keep the qualified name amx_attn_h128g4:: at all call sites. No using-declarations for them in amx_attn_h256g4.
- Slot size per model from plugin::attention_kernels, not 8192 bytes for every model.
- 256 arm added to t_amx_dispatch_dtype: the llama fixture built with head_size 256, 4 heads, 1 KV head, scale 0.0625 with no other new code.
- The packer stays a scalar loop like the 128 x 4 packer.

DEVIATIONS AND THINGS THE LEAD SHOULD KNOW
- The three existing test cases of t_amx_numerics now carry the suffix " - shape_128x4" in their names, because they became template cases. I found no consumer of the old names in the repository.
- The 128 x 4 kernels still hold their own inline copies of the transposing store and of the weight rounding. Sharing the two new helpers needs an edit of the 128 bodies, which the task forbids. Flagged for cleanup.
- Index literals 0..3 remain in the unrolled register code of the new kernels, as in the existing kernels. All domain values are named constants with the value in the name.
- task4.sh compiles the benchmark with the optimization and vector flags of tron's build on this server (from gen/compile_commands.json) plus -mamx-tile -mamx-bf16, not with -march=native as task3.sh does. One extra table with -march=native is recorded: the AVX-512 path is 1.3 to 2.7 % faster there, the ratios are within 0.03.
- The benchmark reads scaling_cur_freq itself in the one-cell mode (about every 0.25 s, first second dropped, median). An outside reader could not tell the set-up of the 4 GiB pool from the loop.
- A fourth use, prefill128, was added to the task 4 table. The baseline logs show 128 prompt tokens per user and prefill pass (32 forwards for 4096 tokens with 1 user), so this is the realistic prefill cell. prefill16 and prefill1024 bracket it.
- The pack of the query is not inside the AMX page unit. It is timed alone: 210 ns per token and call.

TASK 4 RESULT (delphi-3b35, CPU 142, 2026-11-21 22:28 to 22:36 UTC; full table in interface_notes)
- Pass rule "1.5 times faster or more with the data in cache": measured 2.34 to 2.72 in the four cache rows. PASS.
- From main memory, one token per page (decode-like): 1.33 to 1.34 times.
- Core clock: AVX-512 loops 2.700 GHz in all 24 loops. AMX loops 2.396 GHz in all 24 loops. The AVX-512 loop with a tile configuration loaded but no tile product running: 2.700 GHz in 6 loops.
- Cross-check of the AVX-512 copy: 4.14 to 4.29 us per page unit stand-alone. The design gives 67 ns of CPU time per K token in full pages for tron (est., line fit), which is 4.29 us per page unit.
- Against the design's factor row "Full-page time of the attention, prefill, Part B" (low 1.6, working 2.3, high 2.9): the stand-alone prefill ratio is 2.34 to 2.65. The design's working value assumed 1.90 GHz. The measured clock is the 2.40 GHz of the high case.
- Load at the start: load average 65.6. Our socket was 1.4 % busy (two compile jobs of ours). The other socket was 42 % busy (user disagg). The hyperthread sibling CPU 286 was 0.0 % busy during the script.

risks: Decode gain is small from main memory. With one token per page and pages from memory the AMX path is 1.33 to 1.34 times faster per page unit (8.43 us against 6.32 us). The memory stall dominates: the stand-alone numbers give about 4.3 us of extra time per unit for AVX-512 and 4.8 us for AMX over the cache regime. The design's decode rule (at most 1.1 % slower) is not tested by task 4.

The AMX clock is 2.40 GHz in a stand-alone loop that mixes 64 tile products with the AVX-512 softmax and update code. Inside tron the same worker also runs bookkeeping, the join and the AVX-512 pages of the pass in progress. That work then runs at the clock of the core, which may be 2.40 GHz instead of 2.70 GHz (hypothesis; a clock reading of one attention worker during a prefill pass of task 5 would confirm or reject it). A loaded tile configuration alone did not lower the clock (2.70 GHz in 6 loops).

The stand-alone prefill ratio (2.34 to 2.65) is a ratio of kernel work per page unit. The design applies its factor only to the full-page time of a pass. Join wait, the pages the pass writes and waits for K and V are outside this number.

With 1024 query tokens per page the AMX path is 13 to 18 % slower per unit than with 16 tokens (1.80 to 1.83 us against 1.52 to 1.56 us). The packed queries are then 8 MiB per page visit and do not fit the 2 MiB L2. The campaign runs use 128 tokens per user and pass (1 MiB), where the cost is 3 to 5 %.

Memory: the packed-query array of one attention worker is now up to 8 MiB (1024 slots of 8192 bytes) for a model with a 256 x 4 kernel, against 4 MiB before. With 40 attention workers that is up to 320 MiB. The array is zero-filled once when it grows and is never shrunk.

The grow-only resize also changes 128 x 4 models: their slots are no longer zero-filled again after a small minibatch. The padding columns stay zero because both packers write columns 0..3 only. No numeric effect is expected; no 128 x 4 model was run in tron here, only the 128 unit tests.

The wider gate moves every model with a 256 x 4 attention kernel on a bf16 executor to the AMX path in builds with TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON, including the deb preset. Their attention numerics change inside the documented band (weights rounded to nearest even, other add order). Which other registered models have this shape was not determined.

Numerics seen in the benchmark self-check with random data: after 3 pages 676 of 1024 bf16 words of the running sums differ between the two paths, by at most 0.0625 at a largest value of 12.2. This is the known weight-rounding difference. Its size on real model data is not measured.

AMX timings of the cache cells vary more between processes than between rounds of one process (table runs 1.52 to 1.56 us for prefill16; 4 s loop means 1.53 to 1.69 us; one loop of prefill128 read 1.94 us). Cause not determined. Even the slowest reading keeps the cache ratio above 2.1.
The kernel tests execute AMX only on a CPU with AMX. On another CI runner they pass by printing a warning. The new cases have the same property as the existing ones.

The benchmark is a hand copy of tron's instruction patterns, not tron code. The AMX kernels in it were compared line by line with amx_attn.cpp (same tile instructions and loop bounds). If the kernels in tron change, the copy must be updated by hand.

The results files under exec/results/gdn-impl-20261121/bench were written while other agents of this campaign could start builds on CPUs 96-135 of the same socket. The load snapshot covers only the start (socket 1.4 % busy).
